statement: You are given a directed acyclic graph, made of a vertex count n (vertices numbered 0 to n − 1) and a list of edges [u, v], each an edge from u to v.

A topological order lists every vertex so that for each edge [u, v], u comes before v. Find one with depth-first search: visit the vertices 0, 1, …, n − 1 in turn, start a DFS from each one not yet visited, and push a vertex onto a stack only after all of its out-neighbours have been finished. Popping the stack gives the order.
Return the order produced this way.

examples.explanation: The DFS from 0 finishes 5, 3 and 1 first, then 4 and 2, and 0 last, so popping the stack yields 0, 2, 4, 1, 3, 5. Every edge points forward in this list.
Vertex 3 finishes first, inside the search from 0; then 0, 1 and 2 finish in turn. Popping the stack reverses that, and 3 correctly comes after all three of its predecessors.
